q: 1. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest division of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernire scale divided by total number of division of primary scale
explain: Least count of a vernier = (value of one main scale division) / (total number of divisions on the vernier scale); this is the smallest reading directly obtainable with the vernier.

q: 2. Intersection is preferred to radiation when ...............
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: The intersection method locates points by the crossing of two rays from different stations, eliminating the need to measure distance to the point physically.

q: 3. While surveying a plot of land by Plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: The key characteristic of plane table surveying is that field observation and plotting are done together at the same time in the field, unlike other methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 4. Locating the position of a plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: The three-point problem is the specific technique of orienting a plane table and fixing the instrument's own station by resection with reference to three known, plotted points.

q: 5. Pick up the method of surveying in which field observations and plotting proceed simultaneously from the following
explain: Plane table surveying is unique in that field observation and plotting are carried out together at the same time in the field.

q: 6. Which one of the following procedures for getting accurate orientation is the most distinctive feature of the art of plane tabling
explain: Resection (particularly the two-point and three-point problems) is considered the most distinctive and skill-demanding feature of plane table surveying, used to orient the table accurately.

q: 7. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: Radiation is the method in which rays are drawn from a single plane table station to each visible (accessible) point, and distances are plotted to scale along these rays, all from one setup.

q: 8. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: chances to miss details are less.
explain: Because plotting is done in the field itself while the ground is in view, there is little chance of any topographic detail being missed, which is a key advantage of plane table surveying.

q: 9. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted, is
explain: The Two-Point Problem is a resection method used to orient the table when only two points are known and available for sighting, but are not necessarily accessible.

q: 10. Which one of the following is known as instrumental error in plane table surveying?
explain: Non-horizontality of the plane table board is an instrumental (equipment set-up) error, as distinct from personal errors like defective sighting, orientation, or centering.

q: 11. While plane tabling in plane and open area, the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: Orientation is the process of keeping the table parallel to the positions it occupied at previous stations, ensuring the map remains geographically consistent.

q: 12. The survey a small area which one of the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: Radiation is the simplest method of plane tabling, where points are located by drawing rays from a single station; it is most suitable for small, open areas.

q: 13. The plotting of small areas which can be commanded from a single station, is usually done on the plane table by the method of
explain: When a small area can be entirely observed and measured from one single station, the method of radiation is used to plot all the points directly from that station.

q: 14. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing the instrument stations only, is a
explain: Resection is specifically used to locate/establish the plane table's own instrument station with reference to already plotted points.

q: 15. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by .............
explain: The intersection method allows the surveyor to plot a point by sighting it from two different stations without actually traveling to the point.

q: 16. Setting up the plane table consists of operations
explain: Basic setup involves getting the board horizontal (levelling) and placing the plotted point exactly over the ground station (centering).

q: 17. The 'fix' of a plane table from three known points, is good, if .............
options: either the right or left station is nearest
explain: A good 'fix' in a three-point problem is achieved when the middle station is closer to the instrument than the other two points.

q: 18. Plane table survey is considered good as compared to other survey since
options: chances to missing details are less
explain: Since plotting happens while looking at the actual terrain, the surveyor is much less likely to omit important features.

q: 19. Placing the table over the station such that the station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on the ground is
explain: Centering ensures the vertical axis of the plotted point and the ground station are aligned.

q: 20. The two point problem is
options: a case of resection method where no ray is required to be drawn from the proceeding station to the instrument station
locating the position of plane table by means of two visible well defined points
explain: It is a resection technique where the table is oriented and located using two known points, often involving an auxiliary station.

q: 21. Three point problem is concerned with
explain: This is a fundamental resection problem specific to plane table surveying.

q: 22. Strength of fix of a plane table is
options: accuracy in locating the position of instrument station by taking observation to three stations
fixity of table while solving two point problem
explain: Strength of fix refers to how accurately the table's position is determined relative to the known points.

q: 23. The fix of table is good when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the middle station is much nearer than other two stations
the angle subtended between two stations is not very small
explain: A good fix requires geometry that avoids 'danger circles' where the position becomes indeterminate.

q: 24. The resection by two point problem as compared to the three point problem
explain: Two-point resection is more cumbersome and usually less accurate than three-point resection.

q: 25. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to fiducial edge only for
explain: Errors due to non-horizontality are minimized or eliminated when the line of sight itself is horizontal.

q: 26. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation is the most efficient way to plot numerous nearby details once the station is established.

q: 27. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: Intersection is preferred in hills where measuring horizontal distance on steep slopes is difficult.

q: 28. Actually which is not the method of plane tabling ?
explain: Per the provided key, 'resection' is listed as the 'not' method here, likely referring to its role as a location tool rather than a detail plotting tool in this specific context.

q: 29. The instrument used for centering the plane table accurately is
explain: The plumbing fork (or U-frame) carries a plumb bob to transfer the ground point to the paper.

q: 30. The orientation of the table is done by
explain: The table can be oriented using a compass (magnetic needle) or by aligning a line with a previously occupied station (back sighting).

q: 31. "Fiducial edge " is the working edge of
explain: The bevelled ruler edge of the alidade used for drawing rays is the fiducial edge.

q: 32. For the revision of an existing survey with the help of plane table we generally use
explain: Resection is used to establish the current position of the plane table on the map by sighting back to points already plotted.

q: 33. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation ensures that the map is correctly aligned with the cardinal directions on the ground, making all lines on the paper parallel to their ground counterparts.

q: 34. In setting up a plane table at any station
options: both leveling and centering are done simultaneously
explain: In modern practice, leveling and centering are performed at the same time to ensure the board is horizontal and the point is accurately represented above the ground station.

q: 35. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: cannot be used in wet climate
details not available while redrawing to different scale
explain: Since the map is plotted directly in the field on a specific scale, it is difficult to reproduce the survey accurately if a change in scale is required later in the office.

q: 36. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation, intersection, and traversing are all primary methods used in plane table surveying to plot the details of a map.

q: 37. The plane table surveying is
explain: Plane tabling is efficient for small scales, isn't affected by magnetic interference (unlike a compass), and generally requires less expensive equipment.

q: 38. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to the fiducial edge only for .............
explain: If the table is tilted, the line of sight and the fiducial edge are only parallel when looking horizontally; any vertical angle will introduce a lateral error.

q: 39. The two point problem and three point problem are methods of .............
explain: These methods allow a surveyor to locate the table's position (resection) and align the table (orientation) simultaneously using known points.

q: 40. Which of the following methods of plane table surveying is used to locate the position of an inaccessible points?
explain: Intersection is the method where a point is located by the intersection of two rays from two different stations, making it ideal for points that cannot be reached.

q: 41. The resection by two point problem as compared to three point problem .............
explain: The two-point problem is more involved and requires an auxiliary station and more sightings, making it more laborious than the three-point problem.
